verdict.rationale: Greptile documents automated PR review that targets bugs. Its v5 release claims it 'catches more bugs, and flags fewer false positives,' TREX runs the branch in a sandbox to find runtime bugs, and noise control and strictness settings suppress low-impact nits. One independent user reports it 'more often than not catches real issues,' though it is 'sometimes overzealous.' Missing for 10: specific evidence of catching logic errors, race conditions, or edge cases; independent benchmarks of precision and recall; more than one hands-on review report.

support.subject: As a developer, the reviewer catches real bugs in my PR — logic errors, race conditions, broken edge cases — not just style nits

citations.quote: v5 is faster, catches more bugs, and flags fewer false positives by running a swarm of narrowly scoped agents in parallel.
TREX runs your PR branch in a sandbox to find the bugs that only show up at runtime.
With noise control, Greptile limits reviews to high-signal insights, skipping low impact or repetitive feedback.
more often than not it catches real issues and gives the author a chance to reply or fix them before another human reviews the PR.
